subject: Discovery recap & technical priorities — latency / concurrency / next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Liu <jacob.liu@infraops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & technical priorities — latency / concurrency / next steps

Hi Jacob — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned on pain, success criteria, and immediate next steps.

Key pain points you flagged
- Interactive search experience currently times out for some sessions when concurrency hits ~150 users; p95 latency rises above 800ms (target is <= 250ms).
- Streaming UX degrades under multi-widget loads (clients see chunking and rebuffering).
- Cost per 1K generated tokens on current infra is spiking due to small-batch overhead.

Current stack you described
- In-house microservices (Go) with a front-end streaming layer.
- Models: custom-tuned Llama variant hosted on cloud GPUs; inference runs in a single-region setup.
- Request routing is per-request (no global prefix cache).

Success criteria the InfraOps team cares about
- p95 generation latency <= 250ms at concurrency 200 with streaming enabled.
- Smooth streaming UX with <= 150ms chunk jitter.
- Cost per 1K tokens reduced by 30% via batching/caching/quantization options without visible quality loss.

Proposed next steps (short timeline)
1) Technical deep-dive (90m) — focus on tail latency, streaming architecture, and KV/prefix caching patterns. Suggested attendees: Rishi (runtime), Marissa (solutions), Jacob + InfraOps infra lead. — Target: Thurs 2026-09-16 10:00am PT
2) Share current traces / a sampling of p95 logs and a single representative prompt set — Jacob to drop to our shared Drive link.
3) Redwood to run a light benchmark (synthetic) against a model variant and share results + recommendations within 3 business days after the deep-dive.

Attachments sent: infraops-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), infraops-map-action-items.xlsx (proposed MAP).

If the above looks right I’ll schedule the deep-dive and send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Thanks — Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0199

Thanks Dylan — this captures the call well. A couple clarifications:
- The 800ms p95 happens primarily on our global search route when we enable autocomplete + long-context mode together (~2–3s in some rare spikes).
- We can extract a representative 24-hour trace and a 30-minute high-concurrency sample for you to profile. I’ll upload to the Drive by EOD tomorrow.

Deep-dive: Thurs 9/16 10am PT works for us. Attendees: me, our infra lead Priya N., and our engineering manager Aaron. We’ll share access for the trace files before the call.

One ask from procurement side: before the deep-dive, can you share a one-page note on deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) with estimated cost ballparks for predictable concurrency? Our finance team wants a rough number to justify the eval.

Appreciate it — Jacob

Subject: Internal: Prep for InfraOps deep-dive — benchmarks, traces, and agenda

Marissa / Rishi — briefing for the Thurs deep-dive (attached is the MAP I sent to Jacob). High-level ask: come ready to discuss runtime knobs and what we can commit to in a POC.

Why this deal matters quickly:
- Large mid-market account with multi-product footprint (search + chat).
- Clear success criteria around p95 and streaming; if we hit targets there’s upside to expand into dedicated reserved capacity.

What I want from Rishi (runtime):
- Short diagnostic checklist: expected tail causes (KV eviction, batching thresholds, kernel stalls), and which metrics we’ll need from their traces.
- A quick synthetic test plan to run on our side during the POC that mirrors their concurrency pattern (concurrency 200, variable seq len up to 2k).

What I want from Marissa (solutions):
- One-pager for procurement: concise hosted vs dedicated vs private with rough monthly cost ranges (ballpark), and notes on security/compliance differences.

Attachments: redwood-latency-benchmarks.csv (sample baseline numbers we can share), infraops-map-action-items.xlsx

I’ll schedule the invite after I get confirmation from Jacob that the attendee list is final.

Thanks — Dylan

Quick note — I drafted the diagnostic checklist and test plan (see attached stub in Drive). Highlights:
- Focus on per-request KV cache hit rates and tail-latency correlations with batch size.
- Add a streaming jitter test: 100 concurrent connections, 2s context window, measure chunk latency distribution.
- We can simulate their worst-case with 200 concurrency + mix of short/long prompts; should give actionable p95 estimates.

I’ll be on the call Thu and will bring the synthetic harness results (small run) within 24 hours post-call.
